@abbyad @browndav I still think we need to decide if we want to save the form if it's invalid (fails validation or is not complete).  If we save the form and respond with an error message to resend then we will have duplicates, which would need to be resolved on Kujua by the admin.  If we reject invalid forms and ask to be completed again, we could potentially lose data or cause grief for the reporter.  We should probably go with one for now.  At this point my suggestion is to have not-too-harsh validation rules and only accept messages/forms that are valid.

1) My error code was specifically to distinguish identical messages. I agree that it looks better without error codes, so I am torn on that because a CHW reports it an error string to their supervisor it may be a case of broken telephone by the time an admin hears about it. That said, the error message is logged in Kujua as a sent message so may not be an issue. Lets stay without error codes.

2) As for whether or not to save the messages, can we have the default to download only those that pass validation? It could be an advanced option to view messages that failed validation.

3a) I like it that you are including the form name in the error message. The error messages I wrote were close to 160 chars so we would need to work that out better to avoid sending response as multiple messages. We could use the form's short name (which should be less than 14 chars) but regardless using the first X chars of name, replacing cut off section with '...'.

3b) Would be easier to read with quotes around form name in the message.

Bump. It'd be great if we could do a couple of additional things here:

First, we should really test the full receive pipeline. Ideally, this would involve us sending a valid Textforms-formatted message to an SMSSync instance, and ensuring that it shows up in Kujua.

Next, we should take a look at the error-handling path -- send a totally invalid Textforms message, or one with missing fields, and make sure that we correctly reject the message by auto-replying (via SMS) with a human-readable error message.

Once we can do these two things, I think we'd be okay to close this issue.

We're currently just planning to use Textforms as a human-writable message protocol. We _could_ support it in the serializer, but it'd probably just bloat the binary (and the SMS messages it generates) with minimal benefit.

The names, locations etc. of government facilities are typically in the public domain, so I wouldn't bother encrypting facility IDs unless/until we have a user story asking for it. Different matter for individual's IDs.

In CouchDB, yes. It's possible to write each row to the response individually in order to stream results back to the client. Use send('data') inside the while loop to do that. The only problem is that in the browser you can't read a streamed response using XHR so you always end up buffering it all in memory anyway. If this is a list function that will be rendered by the browser as well as the server then it's best avoided, if it's just a server-rendered list function then by all means use the send() function instead of accumulating all the rows in memory.

before closing this ticket let's take a minute to outline all the cases we need to support.  and also make sure we have some tests around them.

_1) Valid message test_
Parse/accept valid (required fields exist) textforms message, assert fields on record are created, assert empty .errors, assert positive response is sent. **(done)**

_2) Invalid message test_
Parse/accept invalid (required field is missing) textforms message, assert fields on record are created, assert .errors contains appropriate error objects, assert response is sent with missing fields message. **(done)**

_3) Invalid message sent with missing fields fixed later_
Do invalid message test then send another message with fields fixed
Assert fields on _same_ record are updated
Assert the relevant error objs are cleared from .errors
This test requires a `data_record_merge` field defined on the form **(done)**

_4) Valid message sent with missing fields broken later_
Do valid message test
Assert fields on _same_ record are updated
Assert the relevant error objs are added to .errors
Assert we send a  response message with missing fields message
This test requires a `data_record_merge` field defined on the form **(done)**

Hi @endor,

Answers ahead. I might break this in to a couple posts.

Answer one:

We should probably defer handling of the "localized strings" -- e.g. { en: "foo", de: "foo" } -- to a locale function that, when given a list of preferred locales (ordered by preference), knows how to extract and return the correct string. There may be a huge number of languages later on, so the `foo.en || foo.fr` approach won't scale. Something like:

``` javascript
  var convert = fuunction (_json, _locales) {
    ...
    var string = extract_locale(string_or_object, _locales);
    ...
  }
```

Answer two and three:

Let's use the labels and types provided by the JSON. The muvuku-generated JSON is intended to be a one-time extraction, to get our form definitions out of the legacy muvuku-data.c format and in to something more manageable. We can _definitely_ adjust the JSON form definitions after the fact -- especially if it lets us avoid testing the `validate` keys directly and/or simplifies the `convert` function.

Special characters:

I made a mistake in the legacy-to-json converter, and missed translation of `\11` from the GSM alphabet to UTF-8. I'll check in a fix, and update the .json file. It looks like only the PSI Cameroon file has that problem.

Answer four:

Currently, all fields in Muvuku are effectively optional, because the SIM application allows CHWs to submit incomplete forms (e.g. to avoid data loss when signal or power loss is imminent). We have support for on-handset storage in the Muvuku dev version, which means we can remove the okay-to-send-incomplete-forms thing, and actually start requiring fields.

I think this is another case where we'll want to manually change the JSON after our final legacy-to-json export. Can we have `convert` check for a `required` attribute and -- if it's undefined, is false, or is null -- assume that the field is _not_ required?

Answer five:

Can we do something similar to what we're doing in item four, above? Specifically, let's assume there should be a `title` attribute in the JSON (pick a good place and key for it), and drop back to some kind of sane default if it's not present.

Just like in the other cases, we can manually add them to the JSON files after our final export.

http://dev.medicmobile.org:5984/kujua-base/_design/kujua-base/_rewrite/VPD/data_records.csv?startkey=%5B%220b55865e94fee64a9f709cb10352f74f%22%2C%22VPD%22%2C%22Damak%22%2C%7B%7D%5D&endkey=%5B%220b55865e94fee64a9f709cb10352f74f%22%2C%22VPD%22%2C%22Damak%22%5D&form=VPD&include_docs=true&descending=true&dh_name=Damak
```

becomes:

```
http://dev.medicmobile.org:5984/kujua-base/_design/kujua-base/_rewrite/VPD/data_records.csv?include_docs=true
```

Note that the start/end keys are excluded so that the **new** data can be imported into Klipfolio. The side effect is that without the keys all forms in the db are exported and field columns become meaningless. Therefore you can only import data if your instance has only 1 form.

Essentially what would be useful is a URL for which we have the following params, default values in brackets:

**Necessary:**
- **form** [null] if null return the whole incoming message (structured or unstructured) in a column

*_Nice to have, highest priority at top: *_
- **facility_name** [null] if specified return only reports from that facility. include child facilities if return_child_facilities is true
- **return_child_facilities** [true]
- **include_forms** [false] relevant only if form=null
- **include_messages** [true] relevant only if form=null
- **start_date** [1970]
- **end_date** [2099]
- **descending** [true]
- **include_docs** [true]
- **locale** [en]

The output fields would be similar to what they are now, I'd suggest we have the following:

```
date, sender number, sender name, sender facility, form fields... (or message contents if form=null)
```

Ok, here is how you can set things via query string. All params with a start _ are considered special, and anything else binds to a input for form values to prefill. So the _ params are:
- _hide_topbar - set to true so the dashboard topbar will not be displayed
- _locale - preset the local the form will render in
- _sync_url - set the sync_url value
- _gateway_num - set the gateway number
- _debug - show the debug panel
- _textforms_option - show the textforms checkbox option
- _use_textforms - if set to 'true' then toggle it to on. 

Any other value gets bound to the actual form input. For example: `test_strips_oos=2` will set the test_strips_oos to value 2.

Talked with Milan and Ryan and just wanted to clarify a couple of things.

For this issue, we're looking at letting the user select a particular facility from an autocomplete/drop-down list; we'll use that facility to determine which roles the user should have. For example, selecting "Dave's District" would make the user a district_admin (cascading all of the way down), selecting "Dave's Nation" would make the user a national_office_admin (cascading all of the way down), etc.

Those roles are enforced at the database level. However, they don't differentiate between particular districts, or between particular national offices -- they're based only on the "level".

The UI will use the facility selection to create a "soft" limitation -- the user will see only his/her own facility by default. However, this won't be enforced at the database level. A determined district_admin for "District A" could, using curl or another HTTP client, read/write data belonging to "District B".

There is a way to provide a "hard" limitation at the database level (i.e. instruct the database to disallow writes if a record's facility ID doesn't match the user's facility ID), but it involves manufacturing a role for each facility, and will likely require more effort.

I'm proposing that -- at least for now -- this issue _does not_ include the group generation "hard limit" I just wrote about in the previous paragraph.

After some discussion on IRC we came up with this strategy for first cut which basically adds a form mgmt screen with the following features:

Form upload process for json form definition which includes:
- Validate form code and json object validate on upload.  
- Enforce uniqueness constraint on form codes, compare with installed form codes, form codes in the system need to be unique so one form doesn't overwrite another.
- ability to change form code during upload process to adjust form code if not unique
- form code string should validate with `[\w]+` (1 or more word characters)
- no immediate support for form versioning

List of installed forms with ability to delete or download installed form as nicely formatted JSON file.  Use case is to download an existing form, modify it in a text editor and then upload as a new form.  Several iterations of adding a new form and deleting old forms would allow you to test your system.

Change current set of forms that are shipped with KL build.  Only ship example forms in new builds.  The example forms may or may not be delete-able (not that important).  Main thing is to allow for new JSON form definition uploads.

New forms will get saved somewhere in ddoc.app_settings structure so that they persist on app updates.  Likely maintaining the same structure as ddoc.views.lib.jsonforms which allows form lookup by key/form code.

JSON-Schema/json-edit validation possibly in the future.

There is a potential problem scenario where we start accepting bad data.  Admin starts by creating form ABC and deploying it, people are submitting ABC normally, then admin decides to delete ABC and upload a new ABC with different fields; now we are getting bad data.  For now our answer is "mess with your forms at your peril" or "get it right before you start collecting data".  We need to make the admin user aware of this potential situation. The alternative/fix might be to keep all history of form creation available to the backend so we can check deleted or inactive forms and make sure there are no form code conflicts.

I believe Marc (perhaps with my help; I can't remember to be honest) added this; 'month' is just intended to be a shortcut for a 'select' field with choices [ [1, "January"], ..., [12, "December"] ](properly localized, if necessary).

There are two reasons for this, and one of them is much better than the other:

  (1) Reduces duplication inside of a JSON form when collecting lots of month-related data (e.g. on several forms), and

  (2) The muvuku compiler doesn't (yet) know how to de-duplicate select lists; using the 'month' type causes Muvuku to use a built-in month list, and thus only store a single copy in the binary. This reduces code size, and lets us fit more forms/questions within the ~30KB we have on a parallel SIM.

Is this referring to sub strings in the message, or in the phone number?
Seems like this is done?

Both, I think. In general, most databases build prefix indexes; some databases will let you talk them in to indexing the result of a function (Couch included, in the map step), but in general the number of index entries you'd have to generate would blow up according to (n^2 + n) / 2 -- still O(n^2) per-item; prohibitive in terms of both time and space.

You're left with linear searches, ideally over a subset of the database. There's a couchdb-lucene setting to allow this, but we'll need to be careful with it. Best to _not_ do these kind of linear searches from the client side in javascript.

Splitting the phone number in to chunks and using prefix matching over those chunks is a great idea as it's still O(1) per item. We could probably adapt this strategy to structured SMSs as well, and then we'd avoid the need to use couchdb-lucene's linear-time substring matching option.

Dave

Just some quick terminology background, from the manual and elsewhere: "In DHIS 2 there are three dimensions that describe the aggregated data being collected and stored in the database; the where (organizational unit), the what (data element), and the when (period) [a timestamp]". [There's also a data "value", which is the actual usually-numeric value]. Effectively, an "indicator" (the unit of record for DHIS2) says something like "At Nairobi hospital, we had 100 bathtubs full of morphine as of 10:00am on 4/1/2013". In the database, the "organizational unit" and "data element" for any imported value are identifiers that look like `gP6hn503KUX`; these IDs refer to an existing organizationalUnit or dataElement that's been registered with the DHIS2 system. The DHIS2 system has a dictionary of these, so elsewhere there might be an organizationalUnit record that looks like `[ 'gP6hn503KUX', 'organizationalUnit', 'Nairobi Hospital' ]`.

Highlighting this:

```
We can currently filter messages by specifying url params for start and end date, which filter
based on the Reported Date. This works to reduce the size, but the CSV output does not contain
what a user would expect. Scheduled messages always have a Reported Date based on the report
that generated them, regardless of when the scheduled message actually goes out. For example,
filtering for messages in March will yield those scheduled in March, even if they are only going
to be sent in July. Conversely, it will omit many of the messages actually sent in March since
they are likely associated to a reported date from a previous month.
```

### Requirements
1. We need to be able to return only messages sent within a given timeframe
2. This only applies to message download, not to form and audit downloads
3. By default we will return all messages

### Nice to haves
1. Filtering by any column
2. User friendly durations in date filters, eg: "3 months", interpreted as "between 3 months ago and now"

### Proposal

```
/export/messages?state=sent,pending&stateFrom=20140201&stateTo=20140301
```

Any messages which entered one of the `state`s between the `stateFrom` and `stateTo` dates will be returned.

Essentially we need to get the following for analytics:

"who missed an appointment in last X days" ==> filter on Pending Timestamp between start & end date.
"who has upcoming appointment next X days" ==> filter on Scheduled Timestamp between start & end date.

Since these visualizations will be on a rolling time we will provide delta times.

Here is an example:
`/export/message?filter='Pending Timestamp'&filterFrom=-14&filterTo=+30` to get all messages with a Pending Timestamp value between 14 days ago and 30 days from now.

Example:

```
/export/messages?startkey=%5B9999999999999%2C%7B%7D%5D&endkey=%5B0%5D&tz=-720&reduce=false&filter_state=scheduled&filter_state_from=0&filter_state_to=10
```

So the parameters are:
- `filter_state`: The key for the state. Valid values are: 'received', 'scheduled', 'pending', 'sent', 'cleared', 'muted'
- `filter_state_from`: The number of days to add to the current date to define the minimum. Can be negative. The minimum is rounded down to the start of the day.
- `filter_state_to`: The number of days to add to the current date to define the maximum. Can be negative. The maximum is rounded up to the end of the day.

It is important to note that messages returned may be in a state other than the filter_state value, for example, requesting `scheduled` messages will return messages that were scheduled to be sent within the filter window, but may have since been `sent`.

Just a reminder; Muvuku for parallel SIMs doesn't support UCS-2 or UTF-8 form codes. We also can't (yet) send UCS-2 data in text fields collected by Muvuku, because it cuts the maximum amount of collectable data by more than half -- every field, every delimiter, every header takes twice as much space because the encoding of a single SMS is all-or-nothing.

With respect to Kujua and the muvuku webapp, though, everything should just work. Javascript uses either UCS-2 or UTF-16 internally to represent strings (most engines use UTF-16), and `JSON.parse` should work with UTF-8 encodings out of the box as long as they're representable by that UTF-16 or UCS-2 internal encoding. IIRC, UTF-16 can represent any Unicode codepoint (the top half of Unicode is represented using "surrogate pairs"), while UCS-2 can only represent the bottom half of Unicode (which still usually suffices for any pronounceable human language). In any case, the Nepali alphabet is located at around 2,300 decimal, which means it should... in theory... just work.

Actually, I take that back, there's an important exception: some "characters" are made up of multiple "code units", i.e. keystrokes compine to form a single glyph visually, but they still (in Javascript) count as separate characters: http://es5.github.io/x6.html#x6.

Code that accesses strings character-by-character -- or, say, pulls out the first four characters of a string -- might visually appear to only contain an incomplete prefix of the original string.

Yeah, here are a couple examples from the form of that last exception:

```
> "सुरु ".length
< 5
> "बन्द".length
< 4
```

Closing, was mainly due to couchdb-lucene 0.9.0 not supporting POST.  Opening new issues for additional lucene limitations.

1) Split the patient IDs array and perform multiple queries and combine the data. We'd end up doing more queries on large installs which will be slower, but again, we can solve performance later (eg: generating daily data and caching if we have to).
2) Rewrite everything to use views rather than lucene. This is the proper approach but I think couchdb views are too restricted to accomplish it (which is why I went for lucene in the first place). The problem is when you have to combine data between documents, for example: find all Visit reports for patients that don't have a Delivery report. As map/reduce handles one document at a time I can't see a way to accomplish this.
3) Denormalise the statistics. For example, write a sentinel transform which updates a number_of_visits field on the Registration when a Visit is received. If we denormalise all the data we need for analytics it'll be lightning fast, and simple to query, however as with all denormalisations it's possible for the data to get out of sync with reality (eg: if you delete a Visit, do we decrement the counter in the Registration?)
4) Perform one unlimited lucene/view query to get all required data into node, and then iterate over the data to generate the statistics. This may require too much memory to be practical.
We chose option 1 as the low risk option.
+1 for option 1 – thanks for the thoughtful analysis.

Just a note on option three: the eventual-consistency / lack of atomic update operations in CouchDB would make that even harder, and the consistency would definitely break if a replication operation was attempted.

All the tricks I tried with regards to injection resulted in invalid syntax. With SQL you usually terminate the injection with `--` to comment out the rest of the query, but I don't think there is a comment operator in Lucene. This means whatever the user enters the query ends with `AND district:xyz` which cannot be shortcircuited with a disjunction or ignored with a comment.

Escaping the query while being the safest approach would really reduce the power of the solution. For example, ANC Analytics is using the lucene syntax to show all reports for `patient_id:xyz`.

I worry that if we attempted to write our own syntax it would end up trying to reproduce much of the functionality of the Lucene syntax and we'd be no better off.

I'll detect syntax errors and change the error message to have a link to our help page on query syntax for now, and we can reevaluate if users find the syntax difficult or injection is found to be possible.

@garethbowen  and I decided to:

Only have one changes listener and process all changes on one document and send one update after all transitions have been applied. Reducing amount of changes feed subscriptions reduces latency in processing a change.  We estimate a large gain here because currently each change on a document will trigger all the transitions.  As is, a document that needs 3 updates to be applied will trigger 24 changes if you have 8 transitions.  This would be reduced to one change event and one update event for N transitions, not sure what big O notation would be here but it significantly improves the algorithm.

So what's happening is the `destroy` is called _after_ the new controller is initialised. I think this is by design so you can animate from from one view to another and only when the animation is finished is the destroy called. So the solution here is to only destroy if you're no longer in the same state. For example, if you nav from `messages.content` to another `messages.content` then the new controller has set the new selected and the new title and so on and we should no longer clear it. But if you navigate from `messages.content` to `messages` or `about` then we should clear it because the new controller doesn't know how to clean up the previous controllers mess.

## To disable auto-replies for unstructured messages

1. In `app_settings.json` set `transitions.default_responses` to `false`. 
```js
  "transitions": {
    "default_responses": false,
    // other transitions
  }
```
2. Upload app-settings: `medic-conf --instance project-name.app upload-app-settings`
3. SSH into the instance and restart Sentinel (`sudo svc-restart gardener`)

This issue is caused by a combination of things:

 - Swahili translation for `schedule.anc_lmp` is `\n`
 - `properties` package casts all translation values before returning them, prioritising Booleans and Numbers before Strings
 - `angular-translate` expects all translation values to be Strings
 
The same crash would happen if a translation value would be `true`, `false` or anything that casts to Number successfully. 

I have added a PR which casts all non-string translation values to string before saving them in the database, which fixes the `webapp` crash. 

In this case, particularly, when `properties` casts `\n` to Number, the result is `0` (as with all other whitespace characters), which will be cast to `"0"`, and the reports detail page will end up like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/40767655-d0401d68-64bb-11e8-997c-148bf042be31.png)

I think the translation should be updated as well.

I strongly prefer using relative dates by default and only using absolute dates when there's a specific use case that benefits. This is for several reasons...

- They answer the most common questions users have (eg: "how long ago was this pregnancy registered?", "when did I last visit this user?", etc). There are some use cases that absolute dates answer better but they're less common in my experience (eg: "did this report come in before this other event?")
- They are very easy to scan and understand correctly without making a mistake when trying to answer the above use cases.
- They reduce in specificity as they recede into the past - who cares if a report from three years ago came in at 10.15am?
- They are timezone agnostic. While we always show absolute dates in the user's timezone, two users in different timezones will see a different absolute date, but they will see the same relative date (eg: "30 minutes ago")
- They are shorter so they take up less space and are less likely to wrap to the next line.

In our implementation of relative dates we watch for click, touch, and hover events and show the absolute time in a tooltip so if it's important to know the exact time then this is still possible without taking up any additional screen space.

No the field remains. You have to use an undo report to remove the date_of_death.

The workflow has 2 options: report a death, supervisor/other health official confirms the death, patient is marked as deceased in our app and a date of death is added to their contact doc. OR report a death, patient is marked as deceased in our app and a date of death is added to their contact doc.

For undoing a death, there are also 2 options: request a correction, supervisor/other health official confirms it was a mistake, patient is marked as alive in our app and date of death is removed from their contact doc. OR undo the death, patient is marked as alive in our app and date of death is removed from their contact doc.

Once someone is marked as deceased by the app (i.e. has a date of death) then all actions should be disabled for that person and all tasks about them should be cleared. This will be handled in configuration for now. The only action available for a person who is deceased is "undo death" so you can't actually submit multiple death reports in that case. For SMS, it's a bit trickier, but in that case, I'd assume that the health facility staff person assigned to confirm the death would indicate the date when submitting the death confirmation form. If the CHW submitted another death report, it wouldn't change anything because the confirmation already happened.

These workflows were defined with extensive input from our regional designers and I am confident they are correct. The issue of deleting the report could be handled differently, such as having certain types of reports that can't be deleted or by adding a feature that would remove the date of death if the report were deleted (I suspect the first option would be preferred, though we'd need to confirm).

Finally, there is no intention of allowing this date of death field to be editable by anyone, so we aren't going to expose it in the "edit person" form and we won't be training anyone to remove dates of death in that way. The correct process is to request a correction and confirm that a correction is needed before marking someone as alive again. Death reporting has a specific protocol and is completely different from how pregnancies are tracked and monitored so that's why it's being handled differently.

PouchDB <-> CouchDB replication used endpoints:

- PouchDB listens to CouchDB `_changes` (which we are already filtering)
- When `changes` are received:
	a) `docs` for `changes` which are on 1st rev are requested via `_all_docs` with `keys` parameter
	    - if any of the docs are missing or deleted or a bunch of other conditions, algorithm falls back on getting the `doc` via `GET`
	b) other `docs` are requested via `_bulk_get` (or `GET`, if `_bulk_get` is not implemented in remote CouchDB).
	    - if any of the results return an error, replication is aborted
	c) when results are received, attachments are requested one by one
	    - if any of the attachments errors, replication is aborted
- When PouchDB writes:
	a) remote `_revs_diff` is called with all the revs of updated documents
	b) if any of the revs is missing, remote `_bulk_docs` is called with all missing rev docs
	     - these requests use `new_edits===false` parameter, no results are expected
		
Because we are handling remote `_changes` requests, we make sure that PouchDB will never receive a `doc-rev` pair it is not allowed to see.
Because all `db-doc` read requests (either via `_bulk_get` or simple `db-doc` `get`) in replication are based on `doc-rev` pairs, we can be sure that replication will not be aborted. 
PouchDB does not attempt to read a pair of `doc-rev` which it has received from other sources than `_changes`. 

Side Notes: 
 - PouchDB does not need access to query views directly
 
Afterthoughts:
1. `_revs_diff` is not filtered at the moment. Filtering could avoid a `_bulk_docs` call with a doc which we already know will be forbidden, which is more expensive because of the `doc` content being sent along. 
2. Should the writes we filter be stored somewhere? Similar to conflicts?

Think of all the tools you use. Your computer lets you delete files, git let's you force push, rm lets you rf. 

My philosophy here is that tools exist to enable you to do things. Warnings are definitely useful, but it's really hard to create them in a such a way where they won't just be ignored, and counter-intuitively research has shown making them large, bolder and more obstructive doesn't help, it makes people ignore them more.

@SCdF I think we discussed this before, but what version do you think we should go to? I have a preference for `1.0.0` because that indicates, to me at least, that it's ready for production use. What do you think?

My reasoning / logic around incrementing horti releases so far has been:
 - 1.0.0 would indicate that it was in theory usable by a third party: stand-alone (not baked into api / webapp), not hard-coded to Medic specifically, etc
 - 1.0.0 would indicate that we will *definitely* not break backwards compatibility, as well as supporting forwards compatibility in some form (ie at least having the capacity to understand that this version is too old to pull from this build server, or support this version of a deployable)
 - And until those two things were true (right now they are not true) I was just incrementing minors / patches.
 - Or alternatively, we give up on all those goals and just tag when we go live, but that would be messaging that is contradictory to what people have asked for, and we've spent considerable energy on (ie I added namespace / application because of the above goals, why would we now not care?)

@garethbowen if you feel like that is the incorrect approach then we can change it to whatever you want. I think what I'm doing is right (obviously!) but it's not a hill I even care to get scratched on, let alone die on.

> 1.0.0 would indicate that we will definitely not break backwards compatibility, as well as supporting forwards compatibility in some form (ie at least having the capacity to understand that this version is too old to pull from this build server, or support this version of a deployable)

It means we won't break backwards compatibility without also changing the major. We can absolutely break backwards compatibility whenever we want.

> 1.0.0 would indicate that it was in theory usable by a third party: stand-alone (not baked into api / webapp), not hard-coded to Medic specifically, etc

That's interesting - I've never associated semver with genericness, for example, we semver medic-webapp but it's completely tied to our use case.

> And until those two things were true (right now they are not true)...

I think we have to start ensuring backwards compatibility now that it's going into production.
Closing as ancient.

We are / I am currently endeavouring to maintain backwards compat already, for sure! Arguably to an extreme that is not necessary. Forward is not there yet though (ie we've yet to explode on unknown schema versions), which I still need to do. Mostly though, it's highly baked into Medic stuff still. This is going to naturally change even without others using it: we want to allow for other build repositories so we can run a local one to run E2E tests through, allowing for different apps means we can use it for deploying other server-side tools at medic (reporter?), as well as integration tests where we want to deploy test / fake apps of different configurations.

This ticket is also (and maybe I didn't make this clear) really mostly a note that **we haven't been tagging Horti so far**, which we should start doing, as a matter of process, because it's going to prod. We should, now that I'm thinking about it, start considering release notes and the like as well!

Anyway: you know my very not-important philosophy as noted above, if you feel strongly feel free to ignore / change it, just let me know. IMO semver is really just a shared delusion anyway, we just need to make sure we're all dreaming the same 🙃

There's a slight problem. Because of the heartbeats we're sending, headers may be indeed already sent before we receive an error from CouchDB. So, errored requests which have already sent a heartbeat will have an error body but a 200 status. PouchDB only checks for the status, so it will consider the request successful. 

Continuous replication would not be affected, as PouchDB will keep requesting with the same seq, but initial replication fails: PouchDB considers the replication successful the app tries to go further, and redirects the user to the app /#error page, which might be confusing.

The retry mechanism can be AT-ed by logging in as an offline user on a fresh browser (so you'd trigger initial replication) and drop your connection after assets are loaded. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/43245771-28a1df0a-90b8-11e8-8827-ab9c65394cec.png)

I would throttle the network and CPU beforehand so you have a wider action window. After you reach this point (where there retry button is visible) you should reenable the connection and after one minute you should observe the page refresh for a second attempt. 

To AT the initial replication check, API would have to respond with an error to offline `_changes` calls, which won't happen if everything is alright. 
I've created a branch (called `4741-broken-api`) that makes all offline users calls to API `_changes` to respond with an error after 12 seconds (so after the 1st heartbeat is sent). You can either upgrade `alpha.dev` to this branch or use it locally (please note that offline users won't work on this branch at all, it serves the only purpose of facilitating this test).
You should login as an offline user in a fresh browser (again, triggering initial replication), there is no need for throttling connection or CPU for this, and observe that after assets are loaded, `"Loading app..."` takes roughly 12 seconds and results in the `Loading error, please check your connection.` error. Again, the page should automatically reload after 1 minute.

**Update**: I have deleted my above comments (in case you wonder where they went, because they are no longer true or relevant to the discussion.

I've talked to the CouchDB folks, and reduce functions are partially run at index time and stored (for performance reasons), so:
 - We can't have a reduce with any dynamic time-based logic in there, because it doesn't all run when you query, so a reduce function that only counts reports based on "this month" cannot work
 - We shouldn't upload reduce functions dynamically because they would cause the entire view to re-generate, due to the data structures used by Couch.

In case it's not obvious, this invalidates the reduce function I wrote in the product call earlier this week, because it relied on the code being run completely dynamically every time you requested it.

OK to that leaves us with two real options for this ticket:
 - Keep the contacts_by_last_visited_date view as it is, but no longer reduce on the server side, instead downloading all of the view results locally and "reducing" there. Big downside of this is that you cannot filter by a list of contacts and also filter by date, so you need to download as many entries as your contacts have ever had visits, every time you render or re-render this page.
 - Changing the contacts_by_last_visited_date view, or using some existing / new view, that has a composite key of contactId and lastReportedDate, and run N view calls, one for each contact that you care about, with [contactId, minimumDateAsWorkedOutFromConfiguration], and then run a _reduce on that.

The former is almost certainly the best approach, the latter invoking way more IO than the former (though neither are ideal).

If this was 3.0.0 we could consider a Mango query, but 2.18 will not have support for them.

Given that some of the above will be covered by configuration (eg the mute form, not generating Tasks for muted contacts), I'll try to summarize the changes/features needed, along with some questions before we implement. Once outstanding questions are answered we spawn new issues for individual parts of this issues, or just leave them all part of this one.

### Configurable Field
An field in app_settings that can contain an array of form IDs that mute a contact, and another field for unmuting contacts. We already have a similar fields for muting SMS notifications:
```
"notifications": {
    "off_form": "OFF",
    "on_form": "ON",
```
It makes sense to combine this new muting with the existing muting of SMS notifications since the reasons for muting via SMS should also mean there shouldn't be Tasks in the app for that contact. We should first verify though that this is compatible with how projects use the existing SMS version. If that is the case, this field would need to change from accepting only a single form to _also_ accepting an array of form fields.

### Updating a doc
If a submitted report's form ID is on the mute list then the contact the report is about should get a muted flag (eg `muted: true`). Conversely when a report on the unmute list is submitted, the contact has the muted flag unset (eg `muted: false`, or remove the field). _Note that we've often entertained a similar feature, that of a submitted report updating fields on the contact. Eg setting/updating a person's birthday via a SMS form. It would be a bonus if the way we implement this issue is generic enough or extendable to satisfy other doc updates._

### Rejecting SMS if the person's place is muted
As mentioned in the issue, we cannot have an unmuted person/place in a muted place. We can avoid this situation in the webapp by setting form context accordingly. By SMS however, we'd need to be able to validate the unmute form by checking that no parent of the contact is muted. We likely either need to allow validation on notification reports, and ensure that fields for all levels of the lineage can be accessed, or perhaps just an `event_type` like `patient_not_found` eg `muted_in_lineage`.

### Displaying muted contacts
Amanda has clearly laid out what a muted contact looks like in the list. Curious if this is necessary for the first version of this feature, or if we are better off with a simpler implementation (eg just graying out the contact in the contact list) until we get real project use and feedback of the feature.

### Not showing Tasks for muted contacts
Done via configuration by checking for any muted parent in lineage.

### Muting SMS notifications
Done via pre-exisiting feature to turn notifications off, if we can combine with that feature.

### Modal warning prior to actions on muted contacts
When opening an action form for a muted contact, if the form is not an unmute form then show a modal before continuing eg “This person belongs to a family that is currently muted. Are you sure you want to proceed? Yes/No".

## Some outstanding questions:
- Can we combine this muting with the existing muting of SMS notifications? Perhaps @ngamita or @derickl have some thoughts on this.
- Are muted contacts excluded from Targets? (This is dealt with in configuration, but good to know here)
- Do we need to group muted contacts together, or can they be shown as before but grayed out? Curious to hear more about the design perspective from @amandacilek, and also the dev effort for options.
- Ideally this seems like something we'd want working offline... but is that a requirement? If no, then this can be handled with a transition. If yes... then we need to figure something out!

Hmm.... running multiple `couch2pg` services is not really ideal because 

1. Records from the 2 DBs won't be in sync (in PostgreSQL, you'll have `-info` records for `data_record`'s that haven't sync'd yet or `data_record`'s without `-info` records).
2. It will call `refresh_matviews()` multiple times and that process alone already takes nearly 4h for some projects.  Running `refresh_matview()` multiple times *simultaneously* is going to fry our server.

While not ideal, I could probably live with **`#1`** in the short term because not many partners care about the `-info` records and we could simply set the `COUCH2PG_SLEEP_MINS` for that process to be very short.  **`#2`** concerns me more, though I suppose we could add an env variable (which defaults to `true` if not provided) that says whether or not to call `refresh_matviews()`.
For **`#2`**... I think we could actually use the `V0_4_MODE ` env variable to disable matview refreshes.

## Expected Behavior
**NOTE** I'm only documenting what I know to be important from an Analytics/PostgreSQL standpoint.  Someone else should chime in with acceptance criteria for other relevant functionality.

### CouchDB

_Note: The sub-bullet points below which indicate how the `xxx_replication_date` should be populated are here for clarity only.  The rules for updating these 2 fields has not changed.  The only thing that should change (from a CouchDB standpoint) after this update is the actual location of the `-info` doc_.

- If a **new document** is **created** in the `medic` DB, it's `-info` doc will be created in `medic-sentinel`.  
  - `initial_replication_date` will be set to `now()`.
  - `latest_replication_date` will be set to `now()`.
- If an **existing document** is **edited** and it **doesn't already have** an `-info` doc, the `-info` doc will be created in `medic-sentinel`.
  - `initial_replication_date` will be blank.
  - `latest_replication_date` will be set to `now()`.
- If an **existing document** is **edited** and it **already has** an `-info` doc and that `-info` doc is in the **`medic`** DB, the `-info` doc will be ***moved*** to the `medic-sentinel` DB.
  - `initial_replication_date` will not be updated.
  - `latest_replication_date` will be set to `now()`.
- If an **existing document** is **edited** and it **already has** an `-info` doc and that `-info` doc is already in the **`medic-sentinel`** DB, the `-info` doc, the `-info` doc does _not_ need to move and:
  - `initial_replication_date` will not be updated.
  - `latest_replication_date` will be set to `now()`.

### PostgreSQL

#### Running the new version of `medic-couch2pg` on an existing PostgreSQL database
- A new `source` field is added to the `couchdb_progress` table.
- The existing row in `couchdb_progress` will be updated to set `source` to `medic` (i assume, since this is the `Update Seq` of the `medic` DB).
- A new row will be added to `couchdb_progress` with the `seq` set to `0` and the `source` set to `medic-sentinel` (I assume).
- `couch2pg` runs on both the `medic` and `medic-sentinel` DB
- `couchdb_progress.seq` is updated for both `medic` and `medic-sentinel` sources.
- The structure and content in the `couchdb` table in PostgreSQL should look no different than it did before the upgrade.  Essentially this table should not notice any changes before and after the upgrade.

#### Running the new version of `medic-couch2pg` on a new PostgreSQL database
- Really the only difference from above is that `couchdb_progress` will initially be populated with the two records (one for each `source`) rather than updating the existing one.

**Summary of the MVP**
- Create a new page on the Admin Console for “Outgoing messages”
- The page should have three tabs: “Scheduled”, “Due”, and “Will not send”
- Each page should have individual messages displayed in a table, with each row showing the details of a particular message
- Messages should be sorted by default by most recent scheduled/due date

![2 tabs mvp - scheduled](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/44803296-e7e58400-ab72-11e8-8203-ce70e0e89411.png)

**Scheduled tab**
- Includes only “scheduled” statuses

![2 tabs mvp - due](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/44803069-2fb7db80-ab72-11e8-88ff-32bbbeb60140.png)

**Due tab**
- This tab contains any messages in a pending/transitory state as well as messages that have been sent (either successfully or unsuccessfully)
- Includes all “pending”, “forwarded-to-gateway”, “received-by-gateway”, “forwarded-by-gateway”, “sent”, “delivered”, “failed” statuses

**Will not send tab**
- This tab contains any messages that will never be sent
- Includes all “denied”, “cleared”, and “muted” statuses


**Table columns**

**Recipient**
- Name of message recipient
- If name is unknown, displays recipient phone number
- If we don’t have name or phone, says “Unknown”

**Created**
- Date (relative) when the original message was generated as part of a schedule. (Devs: Use the reported_date of the form that triggered it.)
- Has a hover tip showing the exact calendar date and time
- Below the created date, display a “View report” link, which opens up that original report on the Medic webapp in a new tab (this is a nice to have but not required).

**Message**
- First line of the message is the title (e.g. “ANC Reminders LMP: Group 1”), in bold
- Full text of the message starts on the second line, wrapping in column as necessary

**Status**
- Message status icon on the left followed by text label on the right
- We have a unique icon for each state (FontAwesome icons for now, size 16px)
- Add a hover tip to provide more definition about what each status means (nice to have)

![screen shot 2018-08-24 at 10 17 03 am](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/44598206-11736980-a787-11e8-81f7-42f915eb5dbd.png)

**Conditional styling of status**
- Whenever a message has a “failed” status, the failed status text and icon should be red
- Any message stuck in a transitional status (pending, forwarded, received, sent) for more than 5 minutes should be styled orange

![screen shot 2018-08-24 at 10 17 44 am](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/44598198-0ae4f200-a787-11e8-99bd-ce73e6c28f84.png)

**Scheduled**
- Date (relative) when the message is/was scheduled to go out
- Has a hover tip with the exact calendar date and time

**Last Update**
- Date (relative) of last state change
- Has a hover tip with the exact calendar date and time

**Note there are three types of dates:**
- Created date (when it was first triggered)
- Scheduled date (when it is due/scheduled to go out)
- Last updated date (date of last state change)

**Date formatting**
- Messages that are “scheduled” will only have two dates - created & scheduled date
- Messages of any other state will have three dates - created, scheduled, and last updated
- All dates should be formatted to show relative dates and times (If the day is today, then it displays information down to the minute e.g. “6 minutes ago”. Otherwise, uses relative language e.g. “3 days ago”, “In 1 month” etc.)
- Whenever we display a relative date, we should allow the user to see a hover tip with the exact calendar date and time (current existing feature on Reports tab)

To enable the specific `goal` (which color codes the number of visits), you need to configure it in `app_settings`. Add the following section: ``` "uhc": { "contacts_default_sort": "", "visit_count": { "month_start_date": 1, "visit_count_goal": 0 } } ``` where: Setting | Default | Accepted values | Description --------------------------------|-------------------|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ contacts_default_sort | empty string | * | *last_visited_date*: default contact sorting will be based on last visited date.
*: default contact sorting will be alphabetical visit_count / month_start_date | 1 | 1-31 | Designates the monthly date when the visit count is reset. visit_count / visit_count_goal | 0 | integer >= 0 | Designates the monthly visit count goal.

To enable default contact sorting to be based on last visited date, you need to configure it in `app_settings`. Add the following section:

```
"uhc": {
    "contacts_default_sort": "",
    "visit_count": {
        "month_start_date": 1,
        "visit_count_goal": 0
     }
}
```

where:

 Setting                        | Default           | Accepted values              | Description                                                                                                                             
--------------------------------|-------------------|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 contacts_default_sort          | empty string | * | **last_visited_date**: default contact sorting will be based on last visited date,  **anything else**: default contact sorting will be alphabetical 
 visit_count / month_start_date | 1                 | 1-31                         | Designates the monthly date when the visit count is reset.                                                                               
 visit_count / visit_count_goal | 0                 | integer >= 0                 | Designates the monthly visit count goal.

> you'd have to look at the clinic and the person to know whether or not the person was muted

Correct

> would be awesome if we were allowing muting of health_centers.

I don't see a good reason why we wouldn't make it generic enough to mute any place level.

> add the muted field to every existing place/contact when they upgrade to the version that includes this feature.

We are unlikely to add a migration for this due to the performance costs (eg rebuilding views, re-downloading all contacts). Given that the absence of a muted flag means that the place is not muted, what is the advantage of adding `muted: false` to places by default?

**Answers to the additional listed questions:**
> 1. For SMS projects, if you submit a P form (for example) for a muted contact, I assume we won't have the "are you sure" workflow. Will we simply accept the P and create the schedule?

Yes, I believe that is the best way to proceed.

> 2. Will we differentiate between ON/OFF and muting when it comes to message states?

The reports that turn notifications OFF set the state of scheduled messages to `muted`. I don't see a reason to have different states... did you have something in mind?

> 3. If a schedule-creating form is submitted (and accepted) for a muted contact, I assume we will still create the schedule but automatically place it in the new mute status?

That is a good point, and I would not have assumed that as it is not how it currently works -- but it is worth specifying as such. In config we should make sure that the response mentions that the patient is muted if that is the case.

> 4. If possible/easy, I can imagine it might help some debugging if we stamp the contact/place's current mute status on the data_record.

Would this be only at doc creation, eg `contact_mute_state_at_creation_time`, or updated whenever the contact's mute state changes, eg `contact_mute_state`?

>> would be awesome if we were allowing muting of health_centers.

> I don't see a good reason why we wouldn't make it generic enough to mute any place level.

Actually... I guess it's less about muting the _place_, but rather muting the _contact_ of that place.  What I'm specifically looking for is the ability to know which CHW's are still with the program and therefore should show up in dropdowns in analytics, for example.  This was discussed in https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/1894 .  This is different than muting the place (`health_center`), which would have the net effect of muting all schedules beneath it.  That isn't what I'm looking for, I just want the ability to mute a specific CHW.

> We are unlikely to add a migration for this due to the performance costs (eg rebuilding views, re-downloading all contacts). Given that the absence of a muted flag means that the place is not muted, what is the advantage of adding `muted: false` to places by default?

The data model (and all our queries) will be much cleaner, not to mention easier to understand for the community, if we can simply check the value of a field that is known to exist rather than having to always check to see if fields exist first, and then check the value of them.  As far as I am aware, we don't have any other situations where the _existence_ of a field is conditional (other than fields being added later, but from that point on they always exist). 

Based on the first part of your response, I recognize we'll have to first check for the existence of that field for projects that have upgraded from a previous version, but ideally all projects that start from this release onwards would have the field no matter what.

> The reports that turn notifications OFF set the state of scheduled messages to muted. I don't see a reason to have different states... did you have something in mind?

Not necessarily... just wanted to understand the plan.  This will make it pretty tricky to know _why_ a particular schedule was muted (OFF message, individual muted, family muted, etc...), but you can figure it out by looking at the timeline of potential mute messages and comparing to the schedule date/time.

> Would this be only at doc creation, eg `contact_mute_state_at_creation_time`, or updated whenever the contact's mute state changes, eg `contact_mute_state`?

I was specifically thinking of the first one (`contact_mute_state_at_creation_time`), but it's not a big deal because technically we can build the timeline of mute messages and I imagine it (creating schedules for muted people) will be pretty rare anyway.

For reference, pasting a summary of a few clarifications discussed with Diana and Jill:

*Do we include outgoing messages from the Messages tab, or just those from the Reports tab?*
- Although we were not initially considering including messages from the Messages tab, we do think that they are a helpful inclusion. They are part of the story of what is happening with the gateway.
- Spam loops should hopefully be avoided because we are including outgoing messages only
- In regards to auto replies - for now, let’s include these in the list and see how it goes. Although we are curious how easy it would be to filter them out.

*Will not send tab - do we include past due date or future due date or both?*
- Ideally, we’d like to include both. If forced to choose, we think displaying messages from the past only is the most helpful. PMs might often want to answer the question “why didn’t X message get delivered?” and they can only answer that by checking both the pending tab (if something has stalled or failed) and by checking messages that were not sent for other reasons such as being muted. Future messages are also helpful to see, especially once we give users the ability to "mute" a scheduled message - we don't want a newly muted message to completely disappear - it should be somewhere accessible. In general, we think ALL message status types should live on this page somewhere.
- Our preference is to add a fourth tab so that we have “Will not send” for all future dates, and “Did not send” for all past dates. We like the tabs because they in essence allow us to “filter” and narrow down the lists without actually having a filter function.

*What to do in cases where recipient phone number doesn’t exist*
- Confirmed that we’re fine just keeping these for now. Jill thinks we have a Google phone number library that we check phone numbers against, and is not sure this will be much of an issue in real life. Let’s see how it goes and address separately if it becomes an issue - at that point we might want to create a new ticket to make this a new status type (as it is a different error, and useful to differentiate from the others).

For my own understanding...
-- will messages which are muted and appear on the "do not send" list switch over to the "scheduled/due" list when the mute status is cleared? And only those after the time when the schedule was unmuted? (i.e. unmute doesn't apply to the entire past schedule, only future messages)
-- for how long do we try again to send failed messages and when do they permanently fail? 
-- did you all run the naming of the tabs and statuses by a few other teammates and users?

> Will messages which are muted and appear on the "do not send" list switch over to the "scheduled/due" list when the mute status is cleared?

Yes, my understanding is that they would switch over to the "Scheduled" tab, provided that the due date is still in the future. If a muted message is unmuted, but the due date is in the past, it should remain in the "Did not send" tab. The rules for which message appears on which tab are based on the message status. A given message may and should move across tabs as it's status changes.

> For how long do we try again to send failed messages and when do they permanently fail?

My understanding is that we do NOT try again. As soon as a message has reached the status "failed" it will not be retried. In the future we would like to add a "resend" button but that has been removed from the MVP.

> Did you all run the naming of the tabs and statuses by a few other teammates and users?

Not explicitly, but during conversation the only status name that was mentioned as confusing was "Delivered". People have a hard time understanding the difference between "Sent" and "Delivered". We suggested that it might be clearer to change "Delivered" to "Received" but I did not include that in this ticket, as it seemed like a separate issue.

Thanks for those clarifications!

The wording that trips me up is "due" in the context of messages that live in the past (because they are no longer due, and arguably the failed ones are "overdue" but cannot be rectified), and "failed" as a status as differentiated from the tab "will not send" (because neither have been sent and neither will... hence my question about re-trying). I'm OK hearing that I'm in the minority here and don't need to make an issue of it if these terms are clear to others.

Here is why we like having "failed" messages grouped together with other pending message states: We anticipate that the "Due" tab will be the tab where PMs spend the majority of their time. They can go to this tab to either verify that all messages are properly moving quickly through the states, or they can be alerted to messages that have failed or been stuck in a pending state for a long time, indicating a potential gateway issue or some other problem. "Failed" is one of the statuses that PMs care about _most_. If we moved "failed" to a different tab, then PMs would have to toggle between multiple tabs to get the full picture of the health of the system.

Your point is valid about the wording "Due" not quite fitting all of the content on that page. All I can say is we're all well aware that this is not a perfect solution. We've had countless back and forth conversations about how many tabs there should be, what should be on them, and what the tabs should be called, and we all compromised to get here. "Due" vs "Overdue" is a tricky concept, because in reality almost every message will take _some_ time to go through the process and be delivered, so I think they will often be past the exact due date/time even when progressing normally through the pending states...Do you have a suggestion for a name besides "Due" without splitting off to make a separate "Overdue" tab?

In the end, we'd just like to get something out, let people start using it, and gather feedback from there to inform future tweaks or iterations. I don't think changing the name of a tab is too difficult down the road!

> because neither have been sent and neither will

On the contrary, "failed" messages DID attempt to send. Here is the full definition of "failed":
**The sending attempt failed.** Sending will not be retried without user intervention.

@garethbowen So here is what's up. Both apps handle two different paths for the same font-awesome resources depending on the trailing slash.

App | Trailing Slash | FontAwesome Url
------------ | ------------- | -------------
WebApp | Yes | http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/fonts/fontawesome-webfont.woff2
WebApp | No | http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/medic/fonts/fontawesome-webfont.woff2
Admin | Yes | http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/medic-admin/fonts/fontawesome-webfont.woff2
Admin | No | http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/fonts/fontawesome-webfont.ttf

Admin paths are "one directory up" from comparable scenarios in WebApp.
Admin with no trailing slash results in 404. All others succeed.

`node_modules/font-awesome/less/variables.less` defines all font-awesome paths as rooted in a relative folder `@fa-font-path: "../fonts"`. This gets compiled into both `medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/css/inbox.css` and `medic/_design/medic-admin/_rewrite/main.css` for the respective apps.  Relative paths in CSS are relative to the location of the CSS file. So the decision to put inbox.css into `css/inbox.css` (while admin is just in `main.css`) is why WebApp is one directory deeper. Then webapp has a ddoc rewrite configured for the additional path when the trailing slash is present (`.../medic/_rewrite/fonts/...`).

So potential improvements:
1. Put medic-admin's `main.css` into `css/main.css` and add a rewrite into webapp-admin's ddoc. Now admin and webapp are the same.
1. Use the grunt *patch* mechanism to set an absolute path like `@fa-font-path: "/webapp-fonts"` and add new api endpoint which redirects to the correct absolute couch path. One path to rule them all.

None are perfect. Inclined to go with 1. The build-time *patch* stuff isn't a super obvious flow. Interested in your thoughts on the best path forward!

## Update on Longpolling issue:

### Background:
For our hosted solutions on AWS (multi-home docker), we utilize an AWS ALB (application load balancer) resources. In our Kubernetes cluster, we deploy a controller which automatically provisions the necessary AWS resource (ALB) and points it to the correct container port living on the docker instances the cluster manages. If a docker node fails, this kubernetes controller will be in charge of re-provisioning the ALB resource to point to the new docker node (that a different kubernetes controller) will be provisioning and re-deploying containers.

The mainstream kubernetes controller deployed to control AWS ALB resources is from CoreOS - [AWS ALB Ingress Controller](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/aws-alb-ingress-controller). This solution did not work for us because the controller during its healthchecks, will poll AWS and verify a variety of services are available. Unfortunately, it will fail and error if [AWS does not have WAF regional service available in the deployed AWS region](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/aws-alb-ingress-controller/issues/439). WAF is an unrelated aws resource to what this controller should be doing. There is a [pending PR](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/aws-alb-ingress-controller/pull/622) to merge a fix which make the controller check which region it is deployed and only verify services that are available in that region prior to erroring out.

Workaround was to deploy a different controller in the kubernetes cluster which would provision the necessary AWS ALB resources. [Zalando](https://github.com/zalando-incubator/kube-ingress-aws-controller) created one which seemed to work fine, but relied on a backend http router daemonset that I deployed in kubernetes cluster called [skipper](https://github.com/zalando/skipper). 

Skipper was causing our failures on gamma.dev. I tried changing multipe configurations for skipper and working with the devs in their Slack channel, but to not luck. I was requested to open up a new issue on their github (still to do).

### Solution:

I pulled Skipper out, and the Zalando Ingress Controller and after multiple other vendor ALB controller deploys, I have resulted in my own scripts setting up the ALB resource until the PR 622 above is merged. This means if a docker node failsover, there is currently a manual step to point the Load Balancer to the new instance. Pulling out the ALB Controller in our kubernetes cluster also impacted how I had planned out our multi-homing solution. Multi-Homing can be done manually through the Console for now, and automation scripts will have to be re-configured to work with the aforementioned ALB solution.

A few considerations
1. At what point is the `V` being considered as 'responding to' an outbound SMS from Medic and when is it an unsolicited Visit.  For example.... if the reminder (`scheduled_task`) from `Medic` went out on 4-October and the `V` came in on 25-October (21 days later), is this `V` really responding to that original reminder from 3 weeks ago or is this `V` really unprompted?
2. When trying to figure out which `scheduled_task` this `V` is responding to, technically we should really only consider `scheduled_tasks` whose `state` is `delivered`, though I'm not sure how reliable those `states` are so we should probably consider `sent` as well.  

I'm not sure what the magic number of days would be for # 1 (perhaps @sarahollis has an opinion), but one option would be to always associate the `V` to the most recently `sent` or `delivered` `scheduled_tasks[n]` where `scheduled_task[n+1].due` is in the future (ie the system hasn't attempted to send the next reminder yet).  If that condition cannot be met, then this `V` will not be associated to anybody.  _NOTE:  Message state descriptions [here](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/user/message-states.md)_

In terms of placement of `report_uuid` I would probably recommend putting the key at the `scheduled_tasks[n]` level, so at the same level as `scheduled_tasks[n].due`.

It was suggested that perhaps we should fix this in the form by having two input groups. One would only show when relevant so that you can select the patient (I'll refer to this group as `user_selected_inputs`), and the other is the traditional `inputs` which would always be relevant, and always hidden. The `inputs` would get values prepopulated, or calculated from the other `user_selected_inputs` section.

I tried two versions of this, but don't think either work, so open to other suggestions!

## Attempt 1: Get patient only in `user_selected_inputs`
The `user_selected_inputs` only has a `db:person` field to get the patient. The `inputs/_id` either gets the value from the app, or "calculated" from 'user_selected_inputs/_id'. We can get the value assigned, but all of the associated fields (eg Name) are not populated. Also, using a calculate on a field has led to problems in the past since prepopulated values could be cleared, especially without _Actions and Events_ (https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/4131) to control when the calculation is done. 

## Attempt 2: Duplicate all inputs to `user_selected_inputs`
This method duplicates all input fields that come from the person's doc into the `user_selected_inputs`, and "copying" over the values to `inputs` when they are filled. This is also subject to the same calculation problem as above, where they would get overwritten. Also, any reference in a label to an input field would need a _third_ copy of the field to refer to.

## Next steps
Are there any other form changes that should be considered?
Would it be worth considering introducing an attribute to specify that a field/group needs to saved regardless of the relevant condition (eg `<inputs mm:always_save='true'>`)? This would be instead of the option 2 above of conditionally hiding a field/group, which seems like it would open a bigger can of worms.

The way I discovered this bug was while writing e2e tests that would check that dates in scheduled messages were being i18ned (https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/4681) when I noticed that whole messages weren't being translated. 

So, you would need a schedule that doesn't use `translationKey`, instead use the old inline `messages` configuration. Then change your configuration so it's effects would be obvious. There are some options here:
- change outgoing messages language (`locale_outgoing`) and have multiple languages listed in the `messages` property of your schedule, your scheduled task would have to respect the language in config
- change the `date_format` or `reported_date_format` and have a date in your message that should respect your format
- change `multipart_sms_limit` and have a super long message that should be truncated to the correct size 

There are other aspects of configuration that affect messages, but these are the most obvious ones. 
I did add an e2e test for this fix and it's testing with `locale_outgoing`.

I was in the field in Togo to check the situation on the ground because CHWs, nurses and supervisors were complaining that the app is too slow.

So when I got to the field, I sought to establish the time taken. First, I asked them how long it took them for a certain action e.g How long it takes to open the Contacts tab when you restart the phone/app.

Starting with CHVs, they mentioned times of around 4-5 minutes from opening the app to the Contacts page and searching for a person. I did the same action with several of their phones and timed it on the Stopwatch app. I got times like this:

          first load after shutdown - 17.26s
          then reports page - 6.12s
          then Contacts Page – 7.10s
          search word 'famille' under Contacts Page - 9.25s 

If you add that up, you get `39.73 seconds`. Of course you consider that they don't press a tab immeadiately it loads so let's take that up to a minute or a bit more. It's still a far cry from the estimated 4-5 minutes. 

As for nurses, they reported 8-10 minutes from startup to getting a patient. The actual times hovered around the below test:

          first load after shutdown - 23.05s
          then reports page - 42.56s
          then Contacts Page - 2min10.51s
          Click 'Zone K1' - 3.46s
          search word 'famille' under Contacts Page 23.14s

This adds up to `3Mins 42.72seconds`. Compare that to 7-10 minutes estimate.

Which leads to the conclusion: there is something about staring at a blank screen with only a spinning animation for more than 10 seconds that makes time elapsed seem more than it actually has.

We should give some feedback to the users. If it took 15 seconds to load the reports tab from shutdown yesterday, it will probably take the same give or take today. So we could use that at least to build the first iteration of this feature.

When processing tombstones, it's important that the tombstone contains actual doc information (otherwise it's useless).
If the doc is deleted via Fauxton, the new deleted rev will be stripped of doc content to keep space low, so when creating the tombstone, to code tries to get the previous rev which would contain data.

I mapped out the Application-Database interactions along with the paint timings for the contact's tab. This is profiling just the scenario for a Muso heavy user experiencing slow performance, so there could be scenarios on the tab not profiled here. In general, things are pretty tight but there are a few optimization ideas below. 

**"Contacts" - Left-Panel**
L1. Get org.couchdb.user:adamayo doc for the facility_id 
L2. Get facility doc associated with facility_id 
L3. Get all the contacts associated with the facility doc

_PAINT THE CONTACTS PAGE WITH SPINNERS_

L4. Use view(contact_by_type) for type "clinic" > Returns all "clinics"  (40 of them for this user)
L5. Get documents of all clinics (max 50 paginated) 
L6. Get clinic doc's primary contact (40) 

_PAINT THE LEFT PANEL_

**"Contact-Content" - Right-Panel**

R1. Get org.couchdb.user:adamayo doc for its facility_id. Select that clinic.
R2. View(docs_by_id_lineage) for the selected clinic. Returns doc in lineage (selected clinic and area doc). 
R3. Hydrate the contacts from these docs. Gets clinic doc's contact and area doc's contact.
R4. View(contacts_by_parent) for the selected clinic. Gets all children's full docs.

_PAINT RIGHT PANEL WITH SPINNER_
XmlForms – Queries for org.couchdb.user:adamayo doc again 
_PAINT RIGHT PANEL FRAMED WITH SECTIONS AND SPINNERS_

R5. View(docs_by_id_lineage) for selected clinic's primary contact. Returns clinic's contact's doc and area's contact's doc.
R6. Fetch clinic's primary contact doc to sort it to top.
R7. Fetch contact information for each of the children from R4  (unsure what this data is used for? Empty in my scenarios)

_PAINT CHILDREN (after 4982)_

R8. View(reports_by_subject) passing in the ids of all children. 
R9. Look up the docs for all the reports 

_PAINT THE REPORTS_


**Optimization Ideas**
Things are pretty good for the left panel. Things are more complicated on the right and my understanding is a bit rough. That said, here are some unmeasured potential optimization ideas:

1. Adjusting when we paint right panel seems like a big win here. Alxndrsn's #4982 
1. ~~Can potentially completely avoid L5 if we just use "Include_docs" for L4.~~ *No measurable gain*
1. ~~Can potentially completely avoid R9 if we just use "include_docs" for R8.~~ *No measurable gain*
1. ~~There are some very small optimizations that can be made in the view map. This is a very small changes, but could reduce time to build views.~~ *No statistically significant improvement*
1. We could paint the left panel after step L5 and lazy load the L6 contacts. Or we could talk about skipping L6 all together if the data is not critical. #4999 #5090 
1. In a similar vein to the above change, we could not populate contact information for the children and completely skip R7. #5098
1. The data fetched in right-panel step R6 was already fetched in step R4. Can we consolidate?  #5103
1. All together, this tab is fetching org.couchdb.user:adamayo 3 times. I assume this document has very low churn and it is likely safe to cache UserSettings() in a similar style to Settings() or Auth() lookups.  #4988
1. ~~Result for L3 is only used in the rare case where the clinic isn't already in the list (must have >50 clinics for this to ever happen). May add more complexity than it is worth, but could avoid L2 and L3.~~ `usersHomePlace.type` is used by `$scope.setLeftActionBar` so this information is required

@SCdF Yes I think it's due to bumping npm to the latest. I think they would consider this a feature as it improves the integrity and reproducibility of the build because it doesn't include random stuff off your disk. So I don't think they're going to fix it in the short term.

That leaves us with a few possible solutions...

1. Publish our shared libs to npm and install them as normal npm dependencies. This is annoying for development if you're making a change in a shared-lib as well as somewhere else in the code as you'll need to publish the shared-lib first. We may be able to find ways to make this easier, such as overwriting the shared-libs with symlinks in development.
2. Do a custom step before calling `npm pack` to replace the file dependencies with inlined code somehow. This feels brittle and too bespoke so easy to forget about or break by accident.
3. Write a custom `npm pack` replacement. I had a quick look at this using the tar `--dereference` flag which inlines symlinks and it worked except because it doesn't understand anything about npm packaging we end up with lots of duplicate dependencies which blows the bundle out from ~5MB to ~30MB. I think it'd be complicated to do this properly.

After weighing these options up I think we should go with option 1 which more closely conforms with how I think npm intends this to be done which means it's more likely to be supported long term.

Agree with 1 being the right option.

I think we can use `npm link` reasonably effectively. This allows easy development, and an example of it would be:
```sh
# First, setup the package to be linked
cd ./shared-libs/bulk-doc-utils
npm link
# Then, link it in API
cd ../../api
npm link @shared-libs/bulk-doc-utils
```
It may be worth scripting this so people don't have to understand it. Especially because if you link it in api and not in webapp you're not really testing it properly.

I'm less sure what to do about travis. On the one hand, we could have it *also* use link, but then we couldn't rework travis to use real builds, because `npm pack` doesn't get fixed by `npm link` (if only!). On the other hand, we should probably be using travis to publish shared libs (and horti, and medic-conf) anyway, because `npm publish` goes off what's on disk not what's in git, so doing it manually is asking for trouble, but I'm not sure how you'd work that in.
